$comment: Neutral shipped <malloc/malloc.h> (Darwin), added by the SQLite-CLI-for-arm64-Darwin cycle. ★ RESOLVER NOTE FIRST, because the filename looks like a collision and is not: resolveSystemDescriptor maps `<stem>.json` PRESERVING the subdirectory (include_path_resolve.cpp:50-53), so `<malloc/malloc.h>` → `malloc/malloc.json` (this file) and `<malloc.h>` → the top-level malloc.json (the pe-only MSVC header) are DISTINCT descriptors that never see each other. The live precedent for the pattern is `<sys/time.h>` → sys/time.json vs `<time.h>` → time.json. ★ WHY A REAL LAYOUT AND NOT AN OPAQUE TYPE: sqlite3.c:28165 is `_sqliteZone_ ? _sqliteZone_->size(_sqliteZone_, x) : malloc_size(x)` — it CALLS through the `size` member, so an opaque `malloc_zone_t` would compile to a fail-loud member-access miss and the whole zone path would be unbuildable. `size` is the ONLY member sqlite touches. ★★ SIZEOF IS 200 BYTES, AND HERE IS EXACTLY HOW THAT NUMBER WAS DERIVED. The full `typedef struct _malloc_zone_t { … } malloc_zone_t;` was read from MacOSX26.4.sdk (extracted read-only at /tmp/apple_sdk_probe/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include/malloc/malloc.h; nothing from the SDK is copied into this repo) and every member counted in order on LP64 (pointer 8, size_t 8, unsigned 4, align 8): THIRTEEN pointer-width members first — reserved1, reserved2, size, malloc, calloc, valloc, free, realloc, destroy, zone_name, batch_malloc, batch_free, introspect — occupying 0..103; then `unsigned version` at 104 (4 bytes), which forces 4 bytes of TAIL PADDING at 108 so the next pointer can 8-align; then ELEVEN more pointer-width members — memalign, free_definite_size, pressure_relief, claimed_address, try_free_default, malloc_with_options, and the five version>=16 typed-memory entries malloc_type_{malloc,calloc,realloc,memalign,malloc_with_options} — running 112..199. 104 + 4 + 4 + 88 = 200, and 200 is already 8-aligned so there is no trailing pad. That arithmetic was then RE-MEASURED, not trusted: an LP64 replica of the struct with every member in order compiled with gcc reports `sizeof=200 align=8 reserved1@0 reserved2@8 size@16 version@104 memalign@112 last@192`. ★ WHY DECLARE THE FULL 200 AT ALL when sqlite only ever holds a `malloc_zone_t *` and never a by-value instance: because a descriptor SHADOWS the real header TOTALLY (include_path_resolve.hpp:60-75, Descriptor → Source → NotFound), including on a NATIVE macOS host where the SDK header is used today via D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK, so the FIRST consumer to write `sizeof(malloc_zone_t)` or to embed one by value would get whatever number we declared — silently. Relying on sqlite's access pattern would make this file correct by coincidence. The three members sqlite needs are declared at their real offsets; the remaining 176 bytes ship as ONE opaque `__opaque_tail` byte array rather than 22 typed function pointers, deliberately: their per-member signatures involve Apple bounds-safety attributes (__sized_by_or_null, __counted_by), a `malloc_type_id_t`, an introspection table, and a `boolean_t` that were NOT independently verified on a real Mac this cycle, and an under-verified callable signature is a silent-miscompile risk in a way that a correctly-sized opaque region is not. Calling any of them fails LOUD as a missing member — the right failure. Tracked at D-FFI-DARWIN-MALLOC-ZONE-TAIL-OPAQUE (closing work: type the tail member-by-member against a measured SDK, keeping the total at 200). ★ THE EXPLICIT `offset` ON EVERY FIELD is the all-or-none explicit-layout channel (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-UNION-OVERLAY, enforced at shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp:2124-2133; the sys/stat.json:120-146 macho-arm precedent). Nothing overlaps here — the offsets are stated so the tail's start (24) and therefore its length (200-24 = 176) are reviewable facts rather than a re-derivation, and so the bare typedef's inline `struct "_malloc_zone_t" { … @off }` body canonicalizes to the SAME TypeId as the `structs` entry, which is what makes `.size` resolve on a value spelled with the bare typedef name. The interner computes size = alignUp(max field extent, align) = alignUp(24+176, 8) = 200. ★ `size`'s signature is `ptr<fn(ptr<void>, ptr<void>) -> u64 "unsigned long">` — `size_t (*)(struct _malloc_zone_t *zone, const void *ptr)` with the self-pointer spelled `ptr<void>`. ★★ THE RETURN TAG IS NOT DECORATION AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED TO `u64`: #47 / D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY makes IDENTITY, not representation, decide the interned TypeId, so a BARE `u64` return mints the ANONYMOUS 8-byte representative while `size_t` on LP64 IS `unsigned long` (stddef.json's `size_t` LP64 arm is exactly `u64 "unsigned long"`, and this file is availableObjectFormats:[macho] where all EIGHT macho formats are MEASURED `dataModel: LP64`, so no `when` variant is needed and none is declared — an ILP32/LLP64 macho target does not exist to disagree). An untagged scalar nested inside `ptr<fn(...)>` makes the WHOLE `Ptr<FnSig>` a DIFFERENT TypeId than the one a user's real `size_t (*)(...)` spells, which is the identical defect fixed at windows.json:324 (`ptr<fn(u32 "unsigned long") -> i32>` for `BOOL WINAPI(DWORD)`) — that one was LIVE because the callback was PASSED as a pointer; this one is latent only because sqlite3.c:28165 CALLS through the member and a call converts the RESULT by value. Latent is not absent: the first consumer to take `&zone->size` or assign it to a declared `size_t (*)(void*, const void*)` would get a fail-loud type mismatch. ⇒ the tag rides on BOTH spellings below — the `typedefs` inline struct body AND the `structs` entry — because they must canonicalize to the SAME TypeId (see the explicit-offset note above); tagging only one would silently split them and `.size` would stop resolving on the bare-typedef spelling (ordinary C pointer coercion accepts the `malloc_zone_t *` sqlite passes, and it avoids a self-referential type), matching how unistd.json and stdlib.json already spell every zone parameter. ★ NO `symbols` AND NO `library` KEY: all seven zone functions this header declares in C are ALREADY shipped and ALREADY export-verified by a real dlopen+dlsym run on an actual Mac ([[D-LK-SQLITE-MACHO-UNDEFINED-LIBSYSTEM-SYMBOLS]]) — malloc_default_zone, malloc_create_zone, malloc_set_zone_name, malloc_size, malloc_zone_malloc, malloc_zone_free, malloc_zone_realloc, at stdlib.json:50-56, all gated [macho]. Re-declaring them would plant a second eager import of each for no gain, and DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every function a descriptor lists, so an unexported name breaks EVERY binary's LOAD (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT, macho exit 127). The consequence, stated rather than hidden: under DSS `#include <malloc/malloc.h>` yields the TYPE but not the FUNCTIONS — a caller must also include <stdlib.h>, which real Darwin does not require. Anchored at D-FFI-DARWIN-MALLOC-ZONE-FN-PROVENANCE. #47 is untouched: MEASURED — `malloc_zone_t` occurs nowhere in shippedLibs today except as prose, and stdlib.json's zone parameters are `ptr<void>`, so this introduces no duplicate typedef and stdlib.json needs no edit. Gated availableObjectFormats:[macho] — an elf/pe #include fails loud (the windows.json:5 [pe] precedent, inverted); zones are an Apple libmalloc concept with no glibc or UCRT counterpart.

typedefs.name: malloc_zone_t
typedefs.type: struct "_malloc_zone_t" { ptr<void> @0, ptr<void> @8, ptr<fn(ptr<void>, ptr<void>) -> u64 "unsigned long"> @16, arr<u8, 176> @24 }
